newsitem.title: FINLAND: New Finnish EMU convergence plan silent on ERM.
newsitem.headline: New Finnish EMU convergence plan silent on ERM.

text.p: Finland's udated convergence programme outlining the path towards meeting the criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU) does not mention the exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
Exchange rate stability is mentioned three times in the 15-page 'Convergence Programme for Finland, September 1996 Update', but ERM not once.
The convergence plan was released on Tuesday together with the five-party government's state budget proposal for 1997.
"The value of the markka has remained stable for a long time," the programme said.

"Finland has good prospects for adhering to a stable value of money even in the future. This requires that domestic cost developments will remain moderate also after the expiration of the general incomes policy settlement in early 1998," it said.

"The stability of the exchange rate can best be secured also in the future by safeguarding that the inflation rate in Finland remains as slow as in other member states with slow inflation and by continuing to follow the economic policy line consolidating state finances," the convergence programme said.
But it offered one clue about what kind of exchange rates the government expects in 1997.
"The exchange rates affecting the value of state debt are estimated to remain at the level prevailing at the end of July 1996," it said, but did not elaborate.

On July 31, the markka closed at 3.0475 against the German mark, at 4.4855 against the U.S. dollar, at 0.6796 against the Swedish crown, at 0.8972 against the French franc and at 6.980 against pound sterling.
Last Friday, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen repeated that a decision whether to link the markka to ERM will be made in the near future.
Some analysts regard ERM membership as a condition for participation in the third stage of EMU due to start in 1999.
